Automating coherent long-form video generation
summary: Google Research introduces a multi-agent orchestration framework built atop Gemini and Veo to generate coherent, multi-minute video narratives, addressing identity drift and cascading failures in current linear AI video pipelines. It comprises four components: AI video co-director (multi-armed bandit-driven global creative optimization, to appear COLM 2026), CANVAS (persistent visual memory for continuity, EMNLP 2026), A²RD (autoregressive segment generation with multimodal memory switching between extrapolation and interpolation), and VQQA (VLM-based prompt refinement using natural-language "semantic gradients").

title: [AINews] The Future of Latent Space
Runway’s WorldPrompt and the Engineering of Real-Time Worlds
summary: Runway’s podcast and blog post detail GWM Worlds 2, a research preview turning video/audio generation into real-time interactive simulation via "autoregressive diffusion." Its key innovation, WorldPrompt, lets users fix elements like the first frame and issue timestamped, real-time actions to control characters, cameras, and environments—positioning Runway against Google’s Genie 3, Odyssey-2 Pro, and World Labs’ RTFM. Runway achieves real-time 720p/24fps video with 48kHz audio via distillation (e.g., 50 denoising steps down to four) after fine-tuning and autoregressive post-training.

Accelerating vision-language models with LFM2.5-VL-DSpark
summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-VL-DSpark, a speculative decoding drafter for their LFM2.5-VL-3B vision-language model, adding just 280M parameters (8.9% overhead) via a 4-layer attention-only drafter with block size 8-9. It delivers decode speedups up to 3.13x on-device (M5 Max/MLX) and 2.66x on H100 (SGLang), with end-to-end gains up to 2.62x and 2.27x respectively, plus day-one support in llama.cpp, MLX-VLM, and SGLang.

title: Efficient MoE Training for Biological Foundation Models
Introducing NV-Reason-CT Open 3D CT VLM for Radiologist Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: NVIDIA released NV-Reason-CT, an open VLM combining a native 3D ViT encoder (Primus/Colipri, 192³ voxels, 13,824 vision tokens with 3D MRoPE) with a Qwen3.5-4B LLM, trained via SFT plus anatomy-aware GRPO to generate radiologist-style chain-of-thought reasoning and structured reports across chest and abdominal CT. It matters because most VLMs mishandle volumetric CT by treating slices as independent 2D images, losing spatial context, and lack auditable multiturn reasoning needed for clinical trust.

Watermarking in vLLM
summary: vLLM has added distortion-free text watermarking using the Gumbel-max trick, fusing pseudorandom generation, Gumbel noise, and argmax into a single GPU kernel within Model Runner v2's sampling pipeline. This matters for provenance tracking of LLM outputs without degrading quality or adding meaningful latency: throughput changes ranged from -1.1% to +2.0% across batch sizes on Qwen3.5-27B. Key engineering solutions include a dual-key scheme to preserve acceptance rates under speculative decoding, and generation-time context deduplication (skipping watermarking on repeated contexts) to avoid degenerate repetition loops, costing at most 0.19% throughput.

Runway’s WorldPrompt and the Engineering of Real-Time Worlds
summary: Runway released GWM Worlds 2 with WorldPrompt, enabling real-time interactive 720p video and audio generation at 24fps. WorldPrompt lets users specify generated worlds and timestamped actions, offering fine-grained control over characters and environments. The system uses autoregressive diffusion and step distillation to achieve real-time performance, though it faces challenges like error accumulation and limited long-term memory. This matters for building interactive simulations for games, robotics, and agent testing. Key takeaway: distilling large diffusion models from 50 steps to 4 steps maintains quality while enabling real-time generation.

Accelerating vision-language models with LFM2.5-VL-DSpark
summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-VL-DSpark, a speculative decoding drafter for vision-language models that achieves 3.13x decode speedup on-device and 2.66x on H100 GPUs with only 280M added parameters (8.9% overhead). The drafter uses the same DSpark architecture as text models, operating on shared hidden-state representations across modalities with a 4-layer attention-only design and block size of 8-9. For VLM builders, this matters because speculative decoding accelerates only decode, not vision encoding or prefill—limiting end-to-end gains to 2.62x on-device where prefill dominates. Day-one support ships in llama.cpp, MLX-VLM, and SGLang with straightforward integration via command-line flags.

title: Efficient MoE Training for Biological Foundation Models
Introducing NV-Reason-CT Open 3D CT VLM for Radiologist Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: NVIDIA released NV-Reason-CT, a vision-language model purpose-built for 3D CT analysis that generates structured diagnostic reports with radiologist-style chain-of-thought reasoning. Unlike general VLMs that treat CT slices independently, it uses a dedicated 3D ViT encoder processing full volumetric data (192³ voxels) with 3D MRoPE to preserve spatial relationships across 300-600 slices. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on CT-RATE (0.614 macro-F1, 0.871 macro-AUROC), outperforming VoxelFM and ClinFusion-8B, while enabling multiturn clinical conversations and audit-friendly explainability. For AI engineers building medical systems, this demonstrates how architectural choices—native 3D processing versus 2D adaptation—fundamentally impact volumetric reasoning quality and clinical trustworthiness.

Watermarking in vLLM
summary: vLLM now supports Gumbel-max watermarking for LLM outputs, embedding provenance signals without distorting generation distributions. The technique uses pseudorandom functions to add reproducible noise to token logits during sampling, allowing detectors with the secret key to verify authenticity. This matters for AI engineers because watermarking enables accountability and copyright protection at production scale. The implementation fuses GPU operations into a single kernel, achieving negligible overhead (−1.1% to +2.0% throughput change) while handling speculative decoding and maintaining output diversity through context deduplication.
